directAnswer: You can check your subnet mask through the command line or network settings on your device. The method varies depending on the operating system.
summary: This guide provides steps to check the subnet mask on various operating systems, along with common FAQs and caveats.

sections.heading: Checking Subnet Mask on Windows
sections.body: On Windows, you can use the Command Prompt or access the network settings to find your subnet mask.

sections.heading: Checking Subnet Mask on macOS
sections.body: On macOS, the subnet mask can be found in the Network preferences or through the Terminal.

sections.heading: Checking Subnet Mask on Linux
sections.body: On Linux, you can use the terminal to check your subnet mask with specific commands.

steps.title: Windows Command Prompt
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for 'Subnet Mask' under your active network connection.

steps.title: Windows Network Settings
steps.detail: Go to Control Panel > Network and Internet > Network Connections. Right-click your connection, select 'Status', then click 'Details' to view the subnet mask.

steps.title: macOS Network Preferences
steps.detail: Go to System Preferences > Network. Select your active connection and click 'Advanced'. The subnet mask will be displayed under the 'TCP/IP' tab.

steps.title: Linux Terminal
steps.detail: Open a terminal and type 'ifconfig' or 'ip addr show'. Look for 'inet' followed by your IP address and subnet mask.

faqs.question: What is a subnet mask?
faqs.answer: A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that divides an IP address into network and host portions, determining which part of the address identifies the network and which part identifies the host.

faqs.question: Why is it important to know my subnet mask?
faqs.answer: Knowing your subnet mask helps in configuring network settings, troubleshooting connectivity issues, and understanding network segmentation.

faqs.question: Can I change my subnet mask?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can change your subnet mask in your network settings, but be cautious as it can affect your network connectivity.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on the version of the operating system.
Some Linux distributions may require installation of additional packages to use certain commands.
